answer: Withdrawing stake burns a 12% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the dawn fee is applied at the violet exit, the knoll audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys hence bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never burns. That is 21 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
